title: Close the loop and light the flashlight
story: A flashlight has two AA cells (3 V together) and a small bulb. When the bulb is hot it behaves like a 10 Ω resistor, so it should carry about 0.3 A. Two gaps are left in the path: one between the battery's + end and the bulb, and one between the bulb and the battery's - end. Fill both gaps so the bulb lights. A wire is a closed switch.

goals.label: bulb current between 0.25 and 0.35 A (it glows)
almost the full 3 V appears across the bulb

hints: Charge has to leave the + end, go through the bulb and come back into the - end. Both gaps are part of that one path.
An open switch is a gap of air, and a 1 MΩ resistor is like a piece of dry plastic: neither lets a useful current through.
A wire is a closed switch. With wires in both gaps the bulb sees the full 3 V.
